newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices rise, volume firms.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices rise, volume firms.

text.p: Traded volume on the Istanbul gold exchange crept upwards to 535 kilos on Monday from Friday's 355 kilos on minor physical demand after weekend jewellery sales, dealers said.
Gold rose in dollar terms to $360.10 an ounce, from $359.30 on Friday following the trend on world markets.
Gold's lira value jumped significantly to 1,289,600 lira per gram, versus Friday's 1,284,100, with the help of the Turkish lira's slide in the local foreign currency markets.
The lira dived to 111,550 to the dollar amid liquidity and the dollar's strength abroad.
Dealers said gold trade remained weak as the market awaited developments in the world markets amid expectations of a bearish trend in the longer term despite the current upward correction.
There was 520 kilos of trade in the morning session, but only 15 kilos in the afternoon when no lira term trade took place. Of the total volume 54.2 percent was in dollar terms.
